TOK PISIN

By Jordan Bissell

Topic:Courts

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:36am

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 5:16pm

Nine-year-old Aiden Guimaraes was killed by a drunk driver in 2024.  (Supplied: Gimaraes family)

A drink driver who hit and killed a nine-year-old boy has been sentenced to 14 years in prison.

Aiden Guimaraes died on the Gold Coast in October 2024 when the e-bike he was on with his father was struck by a mini-van driven by Keith Andrew Chambers.

A spokesperson for Aiden's family says they have "received a life sentence of grief".

A drink driver who hit and killed a nine-year-old boy in front of his family has been handed a 14-year prison sentence.

Aiden Guimaraes was riding an e-bike with his father, David Guimaraes, when Keith Andrew Chambers mounted a kerb and crashed into them in a bike lane in Robina on the Gold Coast in October 2024.

The Brisbane Supreme Court heard Chambers had been drinking heavily the day of the crash, and had spent the afternoon running errands with his partner.

Around 6pm, while Chambers' partner was in the shower, he left her unit without telling her and got behind the wheel of the Honda Odyssey, which was in an "unsatisfactory mechanical condition" and only had one working headlight, the court heard.

Aiden Guimaraes died in October 2024 after the e-bike he was riding on with his father was hit by a car. (Supplied)

Chambers made it just 1.2 kilometres before he hit a centre median strip and lost control of his mini-van, hitting Aiden and his father.

The court heard Aiden suffered severe blunt force injuries, including brain injuries which were "not survivable".

Mr Guimaraes was also seriously injured and was rendered unconscious. He has since undergone multiple wrist surgeries with more to come, and has been diagnosed with PTSD.

Aiden's brother, who was 11 years old at the time, witnessed his brother's death.

Chambers suffered no critical injuries and lied to witnesses at the scene, claiming he had been hit by another car, which he said caused him to lose control of the mini-van.

On the day of the crash, Keith Chambers had been drinking heavily, and had mixed alcohol with painkillers. (ABC News: Mackenzie Colahan)

The 49-year-old's blood was taken around an hour later, with officers estimating that at the time of the collision, his blood alcohol limit would have been between 0.1675 and 0.193, making him "heavily intoxicated".

As well as alcohol, he had Panadeine forte, Endone, and antidepressant Seroplex in his system.

Members of the Guimaraes family and their supporters cried as the father-of-one was being sentenced today.

Justice Glenn Martin said that while he accepted Chambers remained on scene and voluntarily attended a police station the day after the crash, he did not take "serious steps" to address his alcohol and prescription drug misuse until he was in jail.

He also accepted Chambers had pled guilty to all offences, including manslaughter.

Aiden Gimaraes suffered severe blunt force injuries in the crash. (Supplied)

Chambers was handed a 14-year sentence and a six-year sentence, to be served concurrently. He has also been disqualified from driving for life.

He has already served 498 days in pre-sentence custody and is now considered a serious violent offender, meaning he will need to complete 80 per cent of his sentence before he is eligible for parole.

Outside court, family spokesperson Damien Simonfi was flanked by Aiden's parents Andrea and David Guimaraes as he read a statement on the family's behalf.

"Aidan and our beautiful family deserved a future together. Instead, we have received a life sentence of grief."

"One of the most difficult things we've had to face throughout this ordeal was being told the CTP [Compulsory Third Party] insurer valued Aidan's life at just $9,775 — almost exactly the cost of burying him."

The family called for the state government to implement "meaningful change" in the CTP system, such as making repeat offenders of serious driving offences pay more for their CTP insurance.

"Such a practical, uncontroversial change would send a strong signal to offenders. Importantly, [it would] also go a long way in supporting victims' families, throughout the inevitable, financial stress associated with losing a loved one," Mr Simonfi said.

"Choosing to drive, while affected by either drugs or alcohol. It's not an accident. It is a decision."

Keith Andrew Chambers has been disqualified from driving for life. (ABC News)

Aiden's parents thanked media for covering the sentence.

"The DPP did their job. The QPS did their job," Mr Guimaraes said. "What we're worried about is others. No-one should have to go through what we've gone through."
